From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API integration runbook & deep-dive — scheduling

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Our engineering and platform teams at Acme Health would like a technical deep-dive to walk through a proposed integration runbook before we start the pilot. High level we want to cover: SDK auth & session management, streaming behavior and reconnects, function/tool-calling semantics for our actions, and a short runbook for production cutover (deploy checklist, cache priming, rollover).

Can you do a 60–90 minute technical session next week (US time zones)? We are fairly flexible on Tue/Wed morning PT. If useful, I attached a short Acme integration overview (ACME_Integration_Overview.pdf) and a proposed attendee list.

Primary contacts: Mike Turner (platform), devops@acmehealth.com.

Thanks,
Mike Turner
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health
Attachment: ACME_Integration_Overview.pdf (pdf)
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API integration runbook & deep-dive — scheduling

Hi Mike — great to hear. We can absolutely run a deep-dive and draft a short runbook you can iterate on.

Proposed plan (60 minutes + optional 30-minute follow-up slot):
- 10m: introductions & scope (who's on call / success criteria)
- 25m: SDK auth, session lifecycle, and best practices for KV cache priming
- 15m: streaming behavior, reconnects, and bandwidth/latency expectations
- 20m: function/tool-calling patterns and schema examples + Q&A
- Follow-up: 30-min workshop to review your sample prompts and rollout checklist

Slots we have open (PT): Tue 7/20 9:00–10:30am, Wed 7/21 10:00–11:30am, Thu 7/22 8:30–10:00am. Please let me know which works best and I will send a calendar invite and a short runbook draft.

Attaching a first-pass runbook and the internal agenda I’ll use: runbook-v1.pdf, agenda-hosted-integration.md.

CCing Karthik (SDK & streaming) and Lauren (platform partnerships) to make sure we cover platform constraints and contract touchpoints.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Attachment: runbook-v1.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: agenda-hosted-integration.md (markdown)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, Mike Turner <mike.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API integration runbook & deep-dive — scheduling

Thanks Chloe. Quick notes from the SDK/serving side that I want on the agenda so we can be efficient on the call:
- Auth: short-lived tokens vs. long-lived API keys, refresh patterns, header vs. signed-cookie approaches.
- Streaming: typical tokenization latency, early-stop behavior, reconnect semantics; what we do with partial responses and how to resume with KV cache.
- Tool-calls: JSON schema for actions, max payload sizes, recommended retry semantics on idempotent actions.
- Observability: request-level tracing IDs we recommend you pass and how to map them to Redwood console traces.

Link to our internal runbook reference: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-integration-runbook (share for pre-read).

If you can confirm a slot, I’ll add a short checklist we can run through during the session (SDK auth example snippet, sample streaming client code, example tool schema). Also linking this to the HubSpot record for the pilot: hubspot:deal/ACM-4521.

– Karthik
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (will add checklist snippet in calendar invite)
